newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Eight more Timorese enter French Jakarta mission.
newsitem.headline: Eight more Timorese enter French Jakarta mission.

text.p: Eight more East Timorese entered the French embassy in Jakarta on Thursday in an apparent asylum bid, bringing the total number inside the compound in central Jakarta to 16 people, police said.
"Eight more Timorese entered the embassy compound at about 5.30 a.m. They jumped the fence," a policeman on duty at a nearby police post told Reuters.
"The eight that entered the embassy on Tuesday are still inside," he added. The policeman had no further information.
Security officers on duty at the embassy declined to comment when contacted, but Timorese sources said the men who broke into the compound on Thursday were part of an organised asylum bid.

The Jakarta office of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Wednesday the eight men who entered on Tuesday would leave for Portugal, the former colonial power in East Timor, as soon as possible.
It was unclear if the fresh asylum bid would delay their departure.
Since September 1995, 100 East Timorese who have entered foreign embassies in Jakarta have been granted asylum in Portugal.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor and regards Portugal as the administering power in the territory.
The Indonesian government has allowed such asylum seekers to leave for Portugal with the help of the ICRC.
